text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former U.S. deputy secretary of state Richard Holbrooke announces a Dayton-style procedure to handle the Cyprus problem.
- Greek defence minister arrives to debate new ideas to enhance the defence pact Cyprus has with Greece.
- Government announces plans to raise the defence levy.
- British aircraft flies from Akrotiri base to monitor refugee exodus.
- Electricity board inquiry is warned of a power shut-down if a new power station is not built on time.
- The government has told Brussels it will deregulate interest rates while it is telling the public here it still has not taken a political decision.
- The defence pact is our political answer to Turkish expansionism, says Greek Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos. Important decisions are expected to be taken at meeting today.
- Purchase of generators at a new power station depends on the results of an inquiry into tender procedures at the electricity authority, says chairman.
